scenes.text: It's July 6th, 1892, four in the morning, on a river near Pittsburgh.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bank of the Monongahela River at Homestead, Pennsylvania, July 1892, before dawn: two covered wooden barges at a landing, fog on the water, a huge steel mill with smokestacks and a high board fence behind

scenes.text: Two barges slide through the fog, carrying three hundred armed guards.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bank of the Monongahela River at Homestead, Pennsylvania, July 1892, before dawn: two covered wooden barges at a landing, fog on the water, a huge steel mill with smokestacks and a high board fence behind

scenes.text: On the bank, thousands of steelworkers and their families are waiting.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bank of the Monongahela River at Homestead, Pennsylvania, July 1892, before dawn: two covered wooden barges at a landing, fog on the water, a huge steel mill with smokestacks and a high board fence behind

scenes.text: It's your mill. They're your workers. The guards were hired in your name.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bank of the Monongahela River at Homestead, Pennsylvania, July 1892, before dawn: two covered wooden barges at a landing, fog on the water, a huge steel mill with smokestacks and a high board fence behind

scenes.text: By nightfall, at least ten men will be dead.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bank of the Monongahela River at Homestead, Pennsylvania, July 1892, before dawn: two covered wooden barges at a landing, fog on the water, a huge steel mill with smokestacks and a high board fence behind

scenes.text: And you are three thousand miles away, on holiday in Scotland.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Scottish Highlands estate, 1890s: grey stone castle with turrets beside a calm loch, heather hills, a small rowing boat with fishing rods, soft summer light

scenes.text: Six years ago, you wrote that a worker's right to a union is sacred.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Scottish Highlands estate, 1890s: grey stone castle with turrets beside a calm loch, heather hills, a small rowing boat with fishing rods, soft summer light

paper.text: THE RIGHT TO FORM A UNION IS SACRED

scenes.text: You'll become the richest man in the world, then give almost all of it away.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By the end, you'll know the one money rule that got you here,
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: and whether it still works today.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: But to get here, we have to go back. It's 1835, in Dunfermline, Scotland.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: weaver's cottage in Dunfermline, Scotland, 1840: one stone room with a big wooden handloom, rolls of white linen, a small fireplace, a tiny window onto a cobbled lane

scenes.text: You're born on November 25th, in a weaver's cottage. Your name is Andrew.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: weaver's cottage in Dunfermline, Scotland, 1840: one stone room with a big wooden handloom, rolls of white linen, a small fireplace, a tiny window onto a cobbled lane

scenes.text: Keep count of three things: the money, the promises, and who pays for them.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your father, William, weaves fine linen on a handloom in the front room.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: weaver's cottage in Dunfermline, Scotland, 1840: one stone room with a big wooden handloom, rolls of white linen, a small fireplace, a tiny window onto a cobbled lane

scenes.text: Your mother, Margaret, runs everything else.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: weaver's cottage in Dunfermline, Scotland, 1840: one stone room with a big wooden handloom, rolls of white linen, a small fireplace, a tiny window onto a cobbled lane

scenes.text: Then steam-powered looms arrive in town, and they weave faster and cheaper than any man.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: weaver's cottage in Dunfermline, Scotland, 1840: one stone room with a big wooden handloom, rolls of white linen, a small fireplace, a tiny window onto a cobbled lane

scenes.text: Your father's orders stop.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: weaver's cottage in Dunfermline, Scotland, 1840: one stone room with a big wooden handloom, rolls of white linen, a small fireplace, a tiny window onto a cobbled lane

scenes.text: A machine has lowered the cost of cloth, and your family was the cost.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: weaver's cottage in Dunfermline, Scotland, 1840: one stone room with a big wooden handloom, rolls of white linen, a small fireplace, a tiny window onto a cobbled lane

scenes.text: Remember that.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: weaver's cottage in Dunfermline, Scotland, 1840: one stone room with a big wooden handloom, rolls of white linen, a small fireplace, a tiny window onto a cobbled lane

scenes.text: Your mother stitches shoes and opens a tiny shop to keep you fed.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: weaver's cottage in Dunfermline, Scotland, 1840: one stone room with a big wooden handloom, rolls of white linen, a small fireplace, a tiny window onto a cobbled lane

scenes.text: In 1848, she borrows twenty pounds for tickets to America.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: weaver's cottage in Dunfermline, Scotland, 1840: one stone room with a big wooden handloom, rolls of white linen, a small fireplace, a tiny window onto a cobbled lane

scenes.text: Fifty days at sea, in the cheap part of the ship.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You're twelve, and you make friends with the sailors. Your parents mostly hold on.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You land in Allegheny, Pennsylvania: a smoky town across the river from Pittsburgh.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The morning at Homestead is forty-four years away.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: At thirteen, you get your first job, in a cotton mill.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: cotton mill in Allegheny, Pennsylvania, 1848: rows of spinning frames with wooden bobbins, leather belts from the ceiling, baskets of spools, dusty light from high windows

scenes.text: You're a bobbin boy: you change the spools of thread on the machines.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: cotton mill in Allegheny, Pennsylvania, 1848: rows of spinning frames with wooden bobbins, leather belts from the ceiling, baskets of spools, dusty light from high windows

scenes.text: Twelve hours a day, for a dollar twenty a week.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: cotton mill in Allegheny, Pennsylvania, 1848: rows of spinning frames with wooden bobbins, leather belts from the ceiling, baskets of spools, dusty light from high windows

scenes.text: The next job pays two dollars: you tend a boiler in a cellar and oil bobbins.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: cotton mill in Allegheny, Pennsylvania, 1848: rows of spinning frames with wooden bobbins, leather belts from the ceiling, baskets of spools, dusty light from high windows

scenes.text: The smell of the oil makes you sick. You do it anyway.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: cotton mill in Allegheny, Pennsylvania, 1848: rows of spinning frames with wooden bobbins, leather belts from the ceiling, baskets of spools, dusty light from high windows

scenes.text: In 1849, you become a telegraph messenger boy in Pittsburgh, at two fifty a week.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: telegraph office in Pittsburgh, 1850: wooden counter, brass telegraph keys and sounders on desks, paper tape, pigeonholes of message slips, a wall clock, a window onto a smoky street

scenes.text: You memorize every street, and the face of every businessman in town.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: telegraph office in Pittsburgh, 1850: wooden counter, brass telegraph keys and sounders on desks, paper tape, pigeonholes of message slips, a wall clock, a window onto a smoky street

scenes.text: That way, you can hand over a telegram right on the sidewalk.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: telegraph office in Pittsburgh, 1850: wooden counter, brass telegraph keys and sounders on desks, paper tape, pigeonholes of message slips, a wall clock, a window onto a smoky street

scenes.text: Then you learn to read the clicking of the telegraph by ear.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: telegraph office in Pittsburgh, 1850: wooden counter, brass telegraph keys and sounders on desks, paper tape, pigeonholes of message slips, a wall clock, a window onto a smoky street

scenes.text: Almost nobody in the country can do that. Remember that, too.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: telegraph office in Pittsburgh, 1850: wooden counter, brass telegraph keys and sounders on desks, paper tape, pigeonholes of message slips, a wall clock, a window onto a smoky street

scenes.text: On Saturdays, a local man, Colonel James Anderson, opens his library to working boys.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Four hundred books. You borrow one every week.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: It's the only school you have. Remember that.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1853, Thomas Scott of the Pennsylvania Railroad hires you as his telegraph operator.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Thirty-five dollars a month. You're seventeen, and you think you've made it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Two years later, your father dies, still looking for weaving work.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You're nineteen, and now the family depends on you.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1856, Scott offers you a tip: ten shares of a delivery company called Adams Express.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The price is about six hundred dollars. You have nowhere near that.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So you borrow it all: some from Scott, the rest against your mother's house.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Here's the idea your whole life will run on.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: A share is a slice of a company. Think of it as owning one hen on a big farm.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You don't feed the hen. You don't clean the barn. Someone else does.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: But the hen lays eggs, and the eggs are yours. An egg is called a dividend.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Wages stop when you stop working. Eggs keep coming while you sleep.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The catch: hens can die. Then you've lost the hen and the eggs.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: A month later, an envelope arrives with a check for ten dollars.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: It's the first money you've ever made without working for it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You shout: Eureka! Here's the goose that lays the golden eggs.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: Eureka! Here's the goose that lays the golden eggs.

scenes.text: Next, Scott lets you into a company that builds sleeping cars for trains.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You borrow two hundred and seventeen dollars for your share.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Within two years, it pays you about five thousand dollars a year.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: It helps that the railroad you work for is the one buying the sleeping cars.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Today, that would raise questions. In 1858, it raises your income.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: At twenty-four, you run the railroad's whole Pittsburgh division.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1861, the Civil War begins.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You go to Washington with Scott, to run the Union army's trains and telegraphs.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Meanwhile, you put eleven thousand dollars into an oil farm in Pennsylvania.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Oil Creek valley in Pennsylvania, 1862: wooden oil derricks on a muddy hillside, barrels stacked by a creek, a pond of black oil, bare trees, grey sky

scenes.text: In one year, it pays you back nearly eighteen thousand.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Oil Creek valley in Pennsylvania, 1862: wooden oil derricks on a muddy hillside, barrels stacked by a creek, a pond of black oil, bare trees, grey sky

scenes.text: In 1864, the army drafts you.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You pay another man eight hundred and fifty dollars to go in your place.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: It's legal. You don't bring it up much.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The internet says you got rich by working hard in a steel mill. It didn't happen.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By 1863, your income is about forty-two thousand dollars a year.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your salary is twenty-four hundred of that. The rest is eggs.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1865, you quit the railroad for good. You're twenty-nine.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You build iron bridges, and sell American railroad bonds in Europe.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The morning at Homestead is twenty-seven years away.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: December 1868, New York. You sit alone in a hotel room and write a note to yourself.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: room in a grand New York hotel, 1868: writing desk with an oil lamp, pen and a sheet of paper, heavy curtains, a carved bed, gaslight on Broadway through the window at night

scenes.text: You're thirty-three, with an income of fifty thousand dollars a year.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: room in a grand New York hotel, 1868: writing desk with an oil lamp, pen and a sheet of paper, heavy curtains, a carved bed, gaslight on Broadway through the window at night

paper.text: THIRTY-THREE AND AN INCOME OF $50,000 PER ANNUM

scenes.text: You write that the amassing of wealth is one of the worst species of idolatry.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: room in a grand New York hotel, 1868: writing desk with an oil lamp, pen and a sheet of paper, heavy curtains, a carved bed, gaslight on Broadway through the window at night

quote.text: The amassing of wealth is one of the worst species of idolatry.

scenes.text: Idolatry: worshipping the wrong thing. In this case, money.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: room in a grand New York hotel, 1868: writing desk with an oil lamp, pen and a sheet of paper, heavy curtains, a carved bed, gaslight on Broadway through the window at night

scenes.text: The plan: work two more years, then stop, study at Oxford, and give the extra away.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: room in a grand New York hotel, 1868: writing desk with an oil lamp, pen and a sheet of paper, heavy curtains, a carved bed, gaslight on Broadway through the window at night

scenes.text: Remember that.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: room in a grand New York hotel, 1868: writing desk with an oil lamp, pen and a sheet of paper, heavy curtains, a carved bed, gaslight on Broadway through the window at night

scenes.text: You keep the note all your life. You ignore it for thirty-three years.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: room in a grand New York hotel, 1868: writing desk with an oil lamp, pen and a sheet of paper, heavy curtains, a carved bed, gaslight on Broadway through the window at night

scenes.text: Because in 1872, in England, you watch a Bessemer converter at work.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bessemer steel works near Pittsburgh, 1875: a giant egg-shaped converter tilting and blowing a fountain of sparks, glowing ingots, iron ladles, brick walls, rails stacked on the floor

scenes.text: A converter: a giant pot that blows air through melted iron.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bessemer steel works near Pittsburgh, 1875: a giant egg-shaped converter tilting and blowing a fountain of sparks, glowing ingots, iron ladles, brick walls, rails stacked on the floor

scenes.text: Twenty minutes later, the iron is steel: stronger, and suddenly cheap.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bessemer steel works near Pittsburgh, 1875: a giant egg-shaped converter tilting and blowing a fountain of sparks, glowing ingots, iron ladles, brick walls, rails stacked on the floor

scenes.text: People think you invented this. You didn't. Henry Bessemer did.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bessemer steel works near Pittsburgh, 1875: a giant egg-shaped converter tilting and blowing a fountain of sparks, glowing ingots, iron ladles, brick walls, rails stacked on the floor

scenes.text: You barely follow the chemistry. You follow the price.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bessemer steel works near Pittsburgh, 1875: a giant egg-shaped converter tilting and blowing a fountain of sparks, glowing ingots, iron ladles, brick walls, rails stacked on the floor

scenes.text: So you sell your other investments, and put nearly everything into one steel mill.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You name it after Edgar Thomson, the president of the Pennsylvania Railroad.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Which is a thoughtful gift for the man who buys the most rails.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Then, in 1873, the banks collapse, and a long depression begins.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Everyone stops building.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You keep building, because workers and materials are suddenly cheap.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The mill opens in 1875. The first order: two thousand rails, for the Pennsylvania Railroad.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bessemer steel works near Pittsburgh, 1875: a giant egg-shaped converter tilting and blowing a fountain of sparks, glowing ingots, iron ladles, brick walls, rails stacked on the floor

scenes.text: Your rule for the mill: know the cost of everything, down to the cent.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bessemer steel works near Pittsburgh, 1875: a giant egg-shaped converter tilting and blowing a fountain of sparks, glowing ingots, iron ladles, brick walls, rails stacked on the floor

scenes.text: Clerks weigh and write down whatever goes into every furnace.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bessemer steel works near Pittsburgh, 1875: a giant egg-shaped converter tilting and blowing a fountain of sparks, glowing ingots, iron ladles, brick walls, rails stacked on the floor

scenes.text: If a new machine saves a dollar a ton, you scrap the old one, even if it's a year old.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bessemer steel works near Pittsburgh, 1875: a giant egg-shaped converter tilting and blowing a fountain of sparks, glowing ingots, iron ladles, brick walls, rails stacked on the floor

scenes.text: In 1875, a ton of rails costs about fifty-six dollars to make.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By the late 1890s, it's about twelve.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1885, you give a class of Pittsburgh students your secret.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Put all your eggs in one basket, and then watch that basket.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: Put all your eggs in one basket, and then watch that basket.

scenes.text: The internet gives that line to Mark Twain. He printed it nine years after you said it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1881, you take on a partner: Henry Clay Frick.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Frick owns the coke: the baked coal that steel furnaces burn.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Soon you own the fuel, the iron ore, and the ships and railroads in between.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Frick is cold, exact, and very good at costs. In 1889, you make him chairman.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1886, your brother Tom and your mother die within days of each other.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You're in bed with typhoid fever, too ill to go to either funeral.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The next year, at fifty-one, you marry Louise Whitfield.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You had promised your mother you wouldn't marry while she was alive.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1889, you publish an essay called Wealth.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: It says a rich man should give his fortune away while he's still alive.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Its most famous line: the man who dies thus rich dies disgraced.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: The man who dies thus rich dies disgraced.

scenes.text: You are extremely rich when you write it. Readers notice.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The morning at Homestead is three years away.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By 1892, the union contract at your Homestead mill is about to run out.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Steel prices are down. You and Frick want wages down, and the union gone.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You sail for Britain, and leave the fight to Frick.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Scottish Highlands estate, 1890s: grey stone castle with turrets beside a calm loch, heather hills, a small rowing boat with fishing rods, soft summer light

scenes.text: In June, you write to him: we are with you to the end.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Scottish Highlands estate, 1890s: grey stone castle with turrets beside a calm loch, heather hills, a small rowing boat with fishing rods, soft summer light

quote.text: We are with you to the end.

scenes.text: Frick builds a fence around the mill, three miles long, with barbed wire on top.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The workers call it Fort Frick.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: He locks them out, and sends for three hundred Pinkerton guards: a private army for hire.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Which brings us back to the river. It's July 6th, 1892.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bank of the Monongahela River at Homestead, Pennsylvania, July 1892, before dawn: two covered wooden barges at a landing, fog on the water, a huge steel mill with smokestacks and a high board fence behind

scenes.text: The barges land before dawn. Nobody agrees on who fires first.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bank of the Monongahela River at Homestead, Pennsylvania, July 1892, before dawn: two covered wooden barges at a landing, fog on the water, a huge steel mill with smokestacks and a high board fence behind

scenes.text: The shooting lasts most of the day. By evening, the guards surrender.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bank of the Monongahela River at Homestead, Pennsylvania, July 1892, before dawn: two covered wooden barges at a landing, fog on the water, a huge steel mill with smokestacks and a high board fence behind

scenes.text: At least seven workers and three guards are dead.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bank of the Monongahela River at Homestead, Pennsylvania, July 1892, before dawn: two covered wooden barges at a landing, fog on the water, a huge steel mill with smokestacks and a high board fence behind

scenes.text: The governor sends eight thousand soldiers. The mill reopens with new men.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The union is finished. Wages fall, and the twelve-hour day stays.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Remember the looms? A machine made your father too expensive.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: weaver's cottage in Dunfermline, Scotland, 1840: one stone room with a big wooden handloom, rolls of white linen, a small fireplace, a tiny window onto a cobbled lane

scenes.text: Now your workers are the cost. And you are the machine.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: weaver's cottage in Dunfermline, Scotland, 1840: one stone room with a big wooden handloom, rolls of white linen, a small fireplace, a tiny window onto a cobbled lane

scenes.text: Later, you'll say it would have gone differently if you'd been there.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Scottish Highlands estate, 1890s: grey stone castle with turrets beside a calm loch, heather hills, a small rowing boat with fishing rods, soft summer light

scenes.text: But you approved the plan in writing. And you, of all people, know how to use a telegraph.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Scottish Highlands estate, 1890s: grey stone castle with turrets beside a calm loch, heather hills, a small rowing boat with fishing rods, soft summer light

scenes.text: That July, an anarchist shoots and stabs Frick in his office.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Frick survives, and finishes the day's paperwork before he goes home.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: One newspaper writes that ten thousand Carnegie libraries couldn't make up for Homestead.
scenes.speaker: narrator

paper.text: 10,000 LIBRARIES WOULD NOT MAKE UP FOR HOMESTEAD

scenes.text: Years later, you write that nothing in your life ever wounded you so deeply.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The mills, meanwhile, have never made more money.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1900, the company's profit is forty million dollars. About twenty-five is yours.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You and Frick fall out over the price of coke, and then over everything.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: He leaves in 1900, after a lawsuit and a shouting match.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That December, your young company president, Charles Schwab, gives a dinner speech in New York.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: He describes one giant steel company that could make everything, cheaper.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The banker J. P. Morgan is sitting beside him, listening.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Morgan asks Schwab to find out your price.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Schwab asks you after a round of golf, when you're in a good mood. Your wife's idea.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The next morning, you take a pencil and write one number on a slip of paper.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Four hundred and eighty million dollars.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Morgan looks at it and says: I accept this price.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: banker's private library in New York, 1901: dark red silk walls, tall carved bookcases, a massive desk, a marble fireplace, a green-shaded lamp

scenes.text: No haggling. The deal creates U.S. Steel, the first company valued at over a billion dollars.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: banker's private library in New York, 1901: dark red silk walls, tall carved bookcases, a massive desk, a marble fireplace, a green-shaded lamp

scenes.text: Your share is about two hundred and twenty-six million dollars, in gold bonds.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: banker's private library in New York, 1901: dark red silk walls, tall carved bookcases, a massive desk, a marble fireplace, a green-shaded lamp

scenes.text: That's roughly eight billion in today's prices, and far more as a slice of the economy.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Morgan shakes your hand, and congratulates you on being the richest man in the world.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: banker's private library in New York, 1901: dark red silk walls, tall carved bookcases, a massive desk, a marble fireplace, a green-shaded lamp

scenes.text: Later, the story goes, you tell him you should have asked for a hundred million more.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: banker's private library in New York, 1901: dark red silk walls, tall carved bookcases, a massive desk, a marble fireplace, a green-shaded lamp

scenes.text: He says you would have got it.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: banker's private library in New York, 1901: dark red silk walls, tall carved bookcases, a massive desk, a marble fireplace, a green-shaded lamp

scenes.text: Remember the hotel note? Retire in two years. It took thirty-three.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: room in a grand New York hotel, 1868: writing desk with an oil lamp, pen and a sheet of paper, heavy curtains, a carved bed, gaslight on Broadway through the window at night

scenes.text: Now for the second half of the note: give it away.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Remember Colonel Anderson and his four hundred books?
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small-town American public library, 1905: reading room with oak tables, tall shelves of books, a librarian's desk, arched windows, children's corner, morning light

scenes.text: You pay for two thousand five hundred and nine public libraries.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small-town American public library, 1905: reading room with oak tables, tall shelves of books, a librarian's desk, arched windows, children's corner, morning light

scenes.text: The deal: you build it, and the town must buy the books and pay the staff.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small-town American public library, 1905: reading room with oak tables, tall shelves of books, a librarian's desk, arched windows, children's corner, morning light

scenes.text: You also give churches more than seven thousand pipe organs.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You're said to joke that it makes the sermons easier to sit through.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: A concert hall in New York. A university in Pittsburgh. Pensions for teachers.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You spend your summers at Skibo, your castle in Scotland.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Scottish Highlands estate, 1890s: grey stone castle with turrets beside a calm loch, heather hills, a small rowing boat with fishing rods, soft summer light

scenes.text: A bagpiper walks around it every morning to wake you up. Guests do not get a vote.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Scottish Highlands estate, 1890s: grey stone castle with turrets beside a calm loch, heather hills, a small rowing boat with fishing rods, soft summer light

scenes.text: The internet says you personally taught your secrets to a young writer, Napoleon Hill.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Scottish Highlands estate, 1890s: grey stone castle with turrets beside a calm loch, heather hills, a small rowing boat with fishing rods, soft summer light

scenes.text: Your biographer searched your papers, and found no sign that you ever met him.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Scottish Highlands estate, 1890s: grey stone castle with turrets beside a calm loch, heather hills, a small rowing boat with fishing rods, soft summer light

scenes.text: Your biggest hope is peace. You pay for a Peace Palace in the Netherlands.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The idea: countries settle their arguments in a courtroom, not on a battlefield.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: It opens in August 1913.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Eleven months later, the First World War begins.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your memoir stops right there. You never see Scotland again.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1919, the story goes, you send Frick a message: let's meet, and make peace.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Frick's reported answer: tell him I'll see him in Hell, where we both are going.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: Tell him I'll see him in Hell, where we both are going.

scenes.text: On August 11th, 1919, you die in Lenox, Massachusetts. You're eighty-three.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Frick dies four months later.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By then, you've given away about three hundred and fifty million dollars.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small-town American public library, 1905: reading room with oak tables, tall shelves of books, a librarian's desk, arched windows, children's corner, morning light

scenes.text: Most of the last thirty million goes to charity and pensions in your will.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small-town American public library, 1905: reading room with oak tables, tall shelves of books, a librarian's desk, arched windows, children's corner, morning light

scenes.text: So how did the man who called unions sacred end up with ten dead on a riverbank?
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The same way he got everything else. He watched the cost.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Here's the money rule.
scenes.speaker: narrator

paper.text: MONEY RULE: ONE BASKET, WATCHED CLOSELY

scenes.text: The rule: put your money and effort where you understand every cost, then pay attention.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: It built your fortune. But most experts today say the opposite: spread your eggs.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Here's why. Say you earn a salary, and keep fifty thousand dollars of savings in your employer's shares.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: If that company falls ninety percent, your savings are five thousand, and your job may go too.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: One basket only works if you're the one holding it.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bessemer steel works near Pittsburgh, 1875: a giant egg-shaped converter tilting and blowing a fountain of sparks, glowing ingots, iron ladles, brick walls, rails stacked on the floor

scenes.text: You owned the mill, set the prices, and read the cost sheets every week.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bessemer steel works near Pittsburgh, 1875: a giant egg-shaped converter tilting and blowing a fountain of sparks, glowing ingots, iron ladles, brick walls, rails stacked on the floor

scenes.text: A hen on someone else's farm is a different deal.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And here's where the rule hurt. Your basket had nearly four thousand workers in it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You watched every cost. Their wages were a cost.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And in July 1892, you weren't even watching.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Scottish Highlands estate, 1890s: grey stone castle with turrets beside a calm loch, heather hills, a small rowing boat with fishing rods, soft summer light

scenes.text: Watch the basket. But remember who's in it.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bank of the Monongahela River at Homestead, Pennsylvania, July 1892, before dawn: two covered wooden barges at a landing, fog on the water, a huge steel mill with smokestacks and a high board fence behind

meta.thumbnail: You, small and white-bearded in a grey suit, holding up a tiny slip of paper in front of a steel mill pouring sparks; text: '$480,000,000'
meta.description:
You start at $1.20 a week in a cotton mill.
You sell out for $480 million, written in pencil on a slip of paper. Then you give it away.

A comedic dramatization of documented history.

factCheck: Born 25 Nov 1835, Dunfermline; father William a handloom weaver, mother Margaret Morrison (Autobiography; Nasaw)
Power looms ended William's trade in the 1840s; Margaret bound shoes and kept a small shop (Autobiography)
Emigrated 1848 on the Wiscasset, about 50 days; passage paid with a borrowed 20 pounds (Autobiography; Wall)
Bobbin boy at $1.20 a week, 12-hour days, 1848; then $2 a week tending a boiler and oiling bobbins; oil smell made him ill (Autobiography)
Telegraph messenger 1849 at $2.50 a week; learned to take messages by ear (Autobiography)
Colonel James Anderson lent his ~400 books to working boys on Saturdays (Autobiography)
Hired by Thomas A. Scott, Pennsylvania Railroad, 1853, $35 a month (Autobiography)
William Carnegie died 1855

Adams Express: ten shares, 1856, about $600 total; Autobiography says his mother mortgaged the house for $500, Nasaw found Scott advanced the money first; first dividend check $10; 'goose' quote from the Autobiography
Woodruff sleeping cars: loan of $217.50; returned about $5,000 a year within two years (Autobiography; Nasaw)
Superintendent of the Western (Pittsburgh) Division 1859, $1,500 a year
1861: organised military railroads and telegraphs in Washington under Scott
Columbia Oil Company (Storey farm): about $11,000 invested, $17,868 returned in the first year (Nasaw)
Drafted 1864; paid a substitute $850 (Nasaw)
1863 income about $42,000, of which $2,400 was salary (Nasaw; PBS timeline)
Left the railroad 1865, age 29; Keystone Bridge; bond sales in Europe
December 1868 memo: 'Thirty three and an income of 50,000$ per annum'; assets about $400,000; plan to retire in two years and study at Oxford; idolatry quote (Wall; Nasaw)
Saw Bessemer plants in England 1872; Edgar Thomson Steel Works at Braddock opened 1875; first order 2,000 rails for the Pennsylvania Railroad
Rail cost per ton about $56 in 1875 and about $12 by 1898: commonly cited figures, cost and price are mixed in some sources (APPROXIMATE)
'Eggs in one basket' said in the 1885 Curry Commercial College address; Mark Twain used it in Pudd'nhead Wilson, 1894
Frick partnership from 1881-82; Frick chairman of Carnegie Brothers 1889
Tom Carnegie and Margaret Carnegie both died autumn 1886 while Andrew had typhoid; married Louise Whitfield 22 April 1887
'Wealth' published June 1889; 'The man who dies thus rich dies disgraced'
1886 Forum essay: the right of working-men to combine is 'no less sacred' than the manufacturer's (paper text is a paraphrase)
Homestead: 'We are with you to the end' is from a Carnegie letter to Frick before the lockout (PBS; History.com); the exact date, usually given as 10 June 1892, was not confirmed online

Homestead: fence about three miles long; lockout from 29-30 June; 300 Pinkertons on two barges, 6 July 1892; deaths usually given as 7 workers and 3 Pinkertons (some counts 9 and 3 or more); about 8,000 militia arrived 12 July
Carnegie was in Britain (letters from Sunningdale, England, then Rannoch, Scotland). 'On holiday in Scotland' on 6 July 1892 follows the usual telling
Alexander Berkman shot and stabbed Frick 23 July 1892; Frick finished the day's work
'Ten thousand Carnegie Public Libraries would not compensate the country' is attributed to the St. Louis Post-Dispatch, 1892; shown as a paraphrase
Carnegie on Homestead: 'Nothing... wounded me so deeply' (Autobiography), reported indirectly
Carnegie Steel profit 1900: $40 million, Carnegie's share about $25 million (Wall)
Frick left 1899-1900 after the coke-price dispute and a lawsuit
Schwab's University Club dinner speech 12 Dec 1900; golf at St Andrews, Westchester, suggested by Louise; pencilled price $480 million; Morgan 'I accept this price' (Hendrick; Wall)
U.S. Steel formed 1901, capitalised at about $1.4 billion; Carnegie's share $225,639,000 in 5% gold bonds
Today's value: about 38x by consumer prices from 1901, so roughly $8 billion; this is a rough CPI basis only
Morgan's 'richest man in the world' congratulation and the 'a hundred million more' exchange are anecdotes from Hendrick (1932)
2,509 libraries (1,679 in the US); 7,689 church organs; the sermon joke is an attribution
Carnegie Hall 1891; Carnegie Technical Schools 1900; teachers' pensions 1905
Skibo Castle bought 1898; a piper woke the household each morning
Napoleon Hill: Nasaw found no evidence the two ever met (Gizmodo, 2016)
Peace Palace opened 28 Aug 1913; war began 28 July - 4 Aug 1914 (about eleven months later); the Autobiography breaks off at the outbreak of war
Frick's 'see him in Hell' reply, 1919: anecdote first printed by James Bridge, no document survives (DISPUTED)
Died 11 Aug 1919 at Shadowbrook, Lenox, Massachusetts, age 83; Frick died 2 Dec 1919
Gave away about $350 million in his lifetime; about $30 million left, most of it to the Carnegie Corporation, charities and pensions
Homestead works employed about 3,800 men in 1892
Money Rule example ($50,000 falling 90% to $5,000) is arithmetic, not a real case
